summary: 1929 Aermotor fire tower in Zaleski State Forest, Vinton County, Ohio; restored; park text says stairs may be climbed at own risk, but a 2020 radio log says the bottom steps were removed; cab locked at a 2019 visit.

facts.design: 60-foot Aermotor tower with 7 by 7 foot metal cab

access.note: Park text, quoted in a 2020 radio log, says visitors may climb the stairs when weather allows, at their own risk. The same log says the tower was closed to climbing during COVID-19 and the bottom flight of steps had been removed. The cab was locked at a May 2019 visit. Current access is unconfirmed.

visit.trail_note: Easy to find, with parking, picnic tables and campfire spots around the tower (2019 visit report).

events.note: Built 1929 per the register and park text. A March 1930 item calls the new towers ready for operation and gives 65 feet.
An October 1934 Chillicothe Gazette item says O.E. Atkinson of Zaleski was occupying the tower

Forest and brush fires in Vinton County were brought under control on Sunday and Monday, and a Hocking County honor camp helped with brush fires reported at the Atkinson Ridge tower, per a Portsmouth Times item

corrections.why: The record's 19.8 m equals 65 feet, the figure in a March 1930 item. The register and the park text give 60 feet.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and park text say 60 feet; a March 1930 item says 65 feet. The story uses 60 feet and reports the older figure.
A March 1930 item says the new towers were ready for operation, which fits a 1929 build.

sources.title: POTA activation log at Zaleski State Forest, quoting the Ohio park website

notes_for_editor: Both ODNR page URLs for this tower returned 404 in the crawl, so the park text is taken from the WD8RIF post that quotes it. The height disagreement is real: 60 feet (register, park text) against 65 feet (1930 item); the record's 19.8 m follows the 65-foot figure, so a correction is proposed. Visitor reports come only from 2010 and 2019. A 2020 radio log says the bottom flight of steps was removed during COVID-19, so current climbing status is unverified and climbable is set to null. Worth checking the current ODNR climbing and access rule before publishing.
